name: Question 14
worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $2$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{5x-3}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{5x-3}{2(x+1/2)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{5x-3}{(x+1/2)}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $-\frac{1}{2}$ | $5$ | $-3$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-\frac{5}{2}$ |
|  | $5$ | $-\frac{11}{2}$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x-3}{(x+1/2)} & =5-\frac{(11/2)}{(x+1/2)} \\  & =5-\frac{11}{2x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{5x-3}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(5-\frac{11}{2x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[5{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x-11{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[5x-\frac{11}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+1|]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[5(1-0)-\frac{11}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|3|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[5-\frac{11\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}] \\  & =\frac{5}{2}-\frac{11}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3).\end{aligned}
$$
